title: Design System: Java学習システム

display.purpose: The single app-title h1 in the header. Appears once per page.

title.purpose: Subsection group headers (level-grid categories, chart titles), always in Text Dim.

body.purpose: Paragraph text, review prose, problem descriptions.

label.purpose: Tab buttons, badges/pills, meta rows, form labels.

code.purpose: The only role for Java source the user reads or writes — code textareas and code-preview snippets. Never used for prose about code.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The only transition duration/easing used in the system: button hover, tab/card border-color changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The system's only filled button style, used for every primary action (save goal, submit review, generate problems).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #2f6fe0; color: #ffffff; border: none; border-radius: 10px; padding: 10px 20px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2159c4; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost / Link Button
components.description: Transparent, text-only button for secondary navigation actions ("もっと見る", back links).
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost">← レベル一覧へ戻る</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #5b8def; border: none; padding: 0; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { text-decoration: underline; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Translucent tint background + tint border + solid semantic text. Used for header widgets, cert badges, score/difficulty badges, and the favorited state.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-block; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-pill-good { background: rgba(62, 207, 142, 0.12); border: 1px solid rgba(62, 207, 142, 0.4); color: #3ecf8e; } .ds-pill-warn { background: rgba(233, 185, 73, 0.12); border: 1px solid rgba(233, 185, 73, 0.4); color: #e9b949; } .ds-pill-bad { background: rgba(239, 91, 91, 0.12); border: 1px solid rgba(239, 91, 91, 0.4); color: #ef5b5b; } .ds-pill-neutral { background: rgba(154, 164, 187, 0.12); border: 1px solid rgba(154, 164, 187, 0.4); color: #9aa4bb; }

components.name: Well Card
components.description: The recessed list-item card used for levels, generated problems, and review-history entries. One layer darker than its parent panel, with a hover border that signals interactivity.
components.html:
配列とコレクション
Silver Lv.33問生成済み
components.css: .ds-card { background: #0b0f18; border: 1px solid #2a3348; border-radius: 10px; padding: 12px 14px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: #5b8def; } .ds-card.ds-card-cleared { border-color: rgba(62, 207, 142, 0.4); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 4px; color: #e6e9f0; } .ds-card-meta { display: flex; gap: 14px; font-size: 12px; color: #9aa4bb; }

components.name: Code Input
components.description: The monospace textarea used for pasting or writing Java code — the one place the Code typography role appears in an editable control.
components.html: <textarea class="ds-input-code" placeholder="ここにJavaのコードを貼り付けてください..."></textarea>
components.css: .ds-input-code { width: 100%; min-height: 320px; resize: vertical; background: #0b0f18; color: #e6e9f0; border: 1px solid #2a3348; border-radius: 10px; padding: 12px; font-family: 'Fira Code', Consolas, 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Primary Tab
components.description: Top-level section nav — underline style, no background fill, active tab in Console Blue.
components.html: <nav class="ds-tab-nav"><button class="ds-tab active">目標</button><button class="ds-tab">問題集</button></nav>
components.css: .ds-tab-nav { display: flex; gap: 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid #2a3348; } .ds-tab { background: transparent; color: #9aa4bb; border: none; padding: 10px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; } .ds-tab:hover { color: #e6e9f0; } .ds-tab.active { color: #5b8def; border-bottom-color: #5b8def; }

components.name: Line Icon
components.description: The signature custom icon set (icons.js) that replaced emoji app-wide: 24×24 viewBox, stroke-width 1.8, round caps/joins, currentColor stroke, optional filled mode.
components.html: <svg class="ds-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="9"/><polyline points="8 12.5 11 15.5 16 9"/></svg>

narrative.overview:
The app reads as a single instrument panel a solo learner sits at after hours: deep navy field, a handful of glowing status widgets across the header (days-to-goal, streak, Silver/Gold badge progress), and one deliberate accent blue reserved for anything the user can act on right now. Nothing else competes for attention — there is no marketing voice, no illustration, no gradient; the interface exists purely to keep one person's study loop legible at a glance.

The mood is calm and focused. Every surface is flat and quiet by default; color is spent only when it means something (an interactive control, a pass/fail signal, a streak). This restraint is what makes the header widgets and score badges pop without the UI ever feeling busy — the palette has almost nowhere else to spend saturation, so when it does, it reads clearly.

Components are understated and utilitarian: thin hairline borders, a single shared corner radius, no shadows, no ornament. The system trusts background-layering and semantic color alone to carry structure and status, the way a terminal or diagnostics panel would rather than a consumer app.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, single-theme console field — three fixed background layers (page → panel → well) instead of light/dark variants.
One interactive hue (console blue); green/amber/red exist only as pass/caution/fail signals, never decoration.
Fully flat — depth comes from borders and background-layer contrast, never box-shadow.
A single custom inline-SVG line-icon set (icons.js) stands in for all iconography; no emoji anywhere in the UI.
One shared corner radius (10px) everywhere, plus a full pill (999px) reserved for status chips.
Monospace type appears only where Java code is actually read or written.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Blue is the only interactive color; green, amber, and red are reserved exclusively for status (pass / caution-or-streak / fail) and never used decoratively.

rules.name: The Two-Weight Blue Rule
rules.body: One hue, two lightness roles: Console Blue stays light enough to read as text/border against Deep Navy; Console Blue Fill / Fill Hover stay dark enough that white button labels clear 4.5:1. Never put white text on Console Blue itself, and never use the Fill shades as text on a dark background.

rules.name: The Monospace Boundary Rule
rules.body: Monospace type appears only where Java source is being read or written (code textareas, code-preview snippets) — even prose that discusses code (problem descriptions, review results) stays in the sans stack.

rules.name: The Layered-Well Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from three fixed background layers and a one-step border-color change on interaction — never from shadows or elevation transforms.

dos: Do use the shared 10px radius on every rectangular surface; reserve the 999px pill radius exclusively for status chips.
Do treat Console Blue as the system's only interactive hue; keep green/amber/red scoped to pass/caution-or-streak/fail meaning.
Do build all iconography from the icons.js line-icon set (24×24, stroke-width 1.8, round caps/joins, currentColor).
Do use the Code typography role only for Java source the user reads or writes; keep review/description prose in the sans body role even when it discusses code.
Do use the Ink Well background to mark anything "one step deeper" than its parent panel, keeping the three-layer stack consistent.
donts: Don't use emoji as UI icons or tab/status labels — this system deliberately replaced its emoji icons with the icons.js line-icon set; never reintroduce emoji glyphs into the interface.
Don't introduce a second interactive accent color; Console Blue is the system's only "this is clickable" signal.
Don't repurpose Signal Green / Warning Amber / Alert Red for anything other than their pass / caution-or-streak / fail meaning — they are status signals, not a decorative palette.
